decision.about: Sidebar.js grab() and layouts/shell/Shell.js grab() are two ~18-line copies of the identical pointer-capture resize gesture (grab, drag, lostpointercapture, dblclick-to-reset), confirmed identical in shape by Sidebar's own 2026-09-18 decision log ('resize mechanism copied from /layouts/shell/ Shell.grab()')

options.why: removes the duplication now, while it is fresh and small, rather than after a third copy makes the refactor touch three call sites instead of two

decision.because: the two files' own comments already admit the copy happened on purpose, on the same day, which is the cheapest possible moment to undo it - waiting means editing three sites later instead of two now
decision.rule: a gesture copied from one file's own comment ('copied from X') is flagged for extraction the same day it is copied, not left for a future cleanup pass

decision.about: three separate classes each implement get/set JSON in localStorage with a try/catch fallback: core/Page's Page.Store (~40 lines, keyed by page url, has patch() and an in-memory Map fallback), core/Sidebar's Sidebar.Store (~13 lines, one shared key), and ext/Saver's LocalStorageSaver (36 lines, queue-based load/write/delete, used by Panel/Workspace, DevBar and Make)

options.say: leave all three, since each already works and each is small
options.why: no risk, but a fourth module that wants localStorage persistence has three inconsistent examples to copy from instead of one

options.say: extract one small class (get/set/patch/clear, try/catch, memory fallback) that Page.Store and Sidebar.Store both become thin wrappers over; leave ext/Saver's LocalStorageSaver separate since its callers want the queue/load/write/delete shape, not get/patch
options.why: Page.Store and Sidebar.Store share an API shape (get/patch) that LocalStorageSaver does not, so unifying those two costs little and unifying all three would force an API mismatch onto one of them

decision.because: Page.Store is already the more complete of the two (prefix-by-url, memory fallback) - Sidebar.Store should become a one-line instance of the same class with its own fixed key, not a second implementation of the same fallback logic
decision.rule: a new class whose whole job is 'read/write one JSON blob to localStorage with a try/catch' reuses Page.Store's shape (or promotes it out of core/Page into somewhere both core/Page and core/Sidebar can import it from) instead of writing a fourth copy

decision.about: layouts/browse/page.js hand-rolls a 644-line card wall + 297-line stylesheet (tier strip, filter chips, card grid) that does the same job as ext/catalog's browse() (216 lines + 73-line css) - bands of cards behind a filter rail - which core/Layout/page.js already proved out for a similar catalogue (2026-09-06 decision log: 'this used to be a near-copy of browse() ... they are options on browse() now')

options.say: leave layouts/browse/page.js as its own implementation
options.why: its 99 catalogue items come from layouts.json, not live Page children, which is a real architectural mismatch with browse()'s current assumption - not a trivial swap

options.say: give the 99 layout entries the same treatment core/Layout/page.js already gives its own catalogue (read that file's adapter first) so layouts/browse can call this.browse(BANDS, tokens, { facets, search }) instead of its own wall/strip/card functions
options.why: the merge has direct precedent in this repo, proving it is buildable, and the size gap (644 hand-rolled lines vs 216 shared lines) is the single largest line-count opportunity this whole study found

decision.because: this exact class of catalogue-is-not-live-children problem was already solved once in this codebase (core/Layout/page.js, 2026-09-06) - reusing that adapter pattern is materially cheaper than re-deriving it, and the verdict/tier prose that makes this page unique (approved/draft counts, wireframe-vs-photo labelling) is untouched by the change since it lives in the card renderer and facets, not the wall-building code being replaced
decision.rule: before hand-building a second card wall with a filter rail, check whether the data can be shaped as page children (or a lightweight equivalent) and call browse() - core/Layout/page.js is the worked example
